 JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this petition U/s 166 of the Motor vehicles Act 1989, claiming compensation amount of Rs.50,00,000/- with costs and interest from date of accident till date of realization, in respect of death of Sri.Umesha who succumbed to injuries on 10.09.2023 in Road Traffic Accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioner are summarized as under:
On 10.09.2023 at about 3.45 p.m., the deceased was proceeding as a pillion rider in the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-S-5715 driven by one Rajanna from Huliyurudurga Village towards Madduru at SH-33 Kunigal-Madduru Main road,
between Krishnappanakoppalu Gate, P.H.Halli at Huliyurdurga Hobli, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur District.
At that time one car bearing Reg.No.KL-11-AW-2431 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against two wheeler in which the deceased was traveling as a pillion rider.
Due to the impact of accident, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.
3. Immediately after the accident the deceased was shifted to CHC Kunigal Hospital, wherein the doctor declared as dead and conducted the post mortem.
The petitioner has incurred amount of Rs.80,000/- towards medical, transportation, funeral and other expenses.
4. Prior to the date of the accident, the deceased was very hale and healthy and he was aged about 50 years.
He was doing Labour work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month from said avocation and he used to contribute all his earnings towards maintenance of his family.
Due to sudden death of deceased, the petitioner has suffered mental shock and agony and their lives has come to stand still.
The petitioners being the son, daughter and mother of the the deceased and they have lost love and affection of the deceased and their lives have become miserable.

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 is owner, respondent No.2 is the policy holder and respondent No.3 is the insurer are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest.
6. After registration of the petition, notices were issued against respondents.
Inspite of service of the notice, the respondent No.1 to 3 have filed their written statements by denying the entire petition averments.
The respondent No.1 to 3 pleaded that the insurance policy was in force as on the date of the accident and liability if any is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further denied the expenses incurred for funeral ceremony.
Further denied the age of the deceased, avocation and income of the said deceased.
Further denied the other contents of the petition.
The compensation has claimed by the petitioners are highly excessive and exorbitant.
They prays to dismiss the petition.
7. In order to substantiate the claim petition, the petitioner No.1 is examined himself as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12.
Thereby the evidence of petitioner side was completed and case was posted for respondent evidence.
The respondent No.3 got marked Ex.R.1 policy copy with consent of the learned counsel for the petitioner as per the order dated 28.03.2025.
On the same day i.e., on 28.03.2025 leaned counsel for the respondent No.3 has submitted that there is no respondent evidence on behalf of respondents.
Hence, prayed to post the case for the arguments.
Prayer was taken on record.

As per the prayer of learned counsel for respondent No.3,
the respondent evidence was taken as closed and the case was posted for arguments.
8. I have heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials available on record.

9. Upon considering rival contentions raised by the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Umesha died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 10.09.2023 at about 3.45 p.m., SH- 33, Kunigal Maddur Main Road, Between Krishnappanakoppalu Gate, P.H.Halli, H.Durga Hobli,
Tumkuru, due to the rash and negligence driving of the car bearing Reg.No.KL-11-AW-2431 by its rider?
2.
Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation?

If so, what amount and from whom?
4.
What order or award?
10. My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1: In the affirmative,

 REASONS

ISSUE NO.1:
11.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that on 10.09.2023 at about 3.45 p.m., the deceased was proceeding as a pillion rider in the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-S-5715 driven by one Rajanna from Huliyurudurga Village towards Madduru at SH-33 Kunigal-Madduru Main road, between Krishnappanakoppalu Gate, P.H.Halli at Huliyurdurga Hobli, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur District.
At that time one car bearing Reg.No.KL-11-AW-2431 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against two wheeler in which the deceased was traveling as a pillion rider.
Due to the impact of accident, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.
12. To substantiate the petition averments, petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 12 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12.
Ex.P.1 is the FIR and complaint which reveals that one Rajanna has lodged complaint on 10.09.2023 against the driver of the respondent offender vehicle bearing Reg.No.KL-11- AW-2431.
Upon the complaint, the police have registered FIR for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC.
The Ex.P.7 is the Inquest report which clearly discloses that, deceased has died on 10.09.2023 in a Road Traffic Accident.
Ex.P.2 to Ex.P.4
are the spot mahazar, seizure mahazar and sketch which speaks about the occurrence of accident.
Ex.P.6 is the PM report which reveals that, deceased has succumbed to the injuries in the said accident.
Ex.P.5 is the IMV reports.

Ex.P.8 is the charge sheet which reveals that, police have investigated the matter and filed charge sheet against the driver of the offender vehicle bearing Reg.No.KL-11-AW- 2431.
13.

Therefore, it is apparent on the face of records that, the respondent has admitted the occurrence of accident and death of deceased has caused due to the rash and negligent drive of the driver of the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KL-11-AW-2431.
In the absence of any cogent materials from the respondents in this regard.
The only inference which has to be drawn is that, the accident in question was the result of the rash and negligent drive of the driver of the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KL-11-AW-2431.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
14.
The PW.1 in his evidence has deposed that, their deceased father Umesha, was doing Labour work and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
His father was aged about 50 years and was hale and healthy before the occurrence of accident.
Petitioner being son, daughter and mother of the deceased, was wholly dependent on the income of the said deceased, he being a sole bread earning member in his family.
He has further deposed that, he has spent amount of Rs.80,000/- towards funeral and other expenses.

sentences.text: Petitioners have averred in the petition that, the petitioner No.1 is the son, petitioner No.2 is the daughter and petitioner No.3 is the mother of the deceased.
To substantiate the same, PW.1 has produced notarized copies of Aadhars card along with originals of himself and petitioner No.2 and 3.
These documents reflects the relationship of deceased with the petitioners.
The oral and documentary evidence led by PW.1 reflects that, petitioners No.1 to 3 are the LR's of deceased.

Since,
the respondent has not contested the said matter in the evidence led by PW.1.
Then the evidence of PW.1 stands unshaken and the same is sufficient to show that petitioner No.1 to 3 are the LR's of deceased.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 In the affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
16.

Basically three facts lead to be established by the claimants for assessing compensation in the case of death as per Sarla Verma Case i.e., (i) age of deceased,
(ii) Income of deceased and (iii) Number of dependents.
( i ) Age of deceased:
According to the petitioners the age of the deceased at the time of the accident was 50 years.
As per the aadhar card marked at Ex.P.12, wherein the date of the birth of the deceased mentioned as 01.01.1972, the accident was occurred on 10.09.2023.
So, as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged 51 years.
(ii). Income of the deceased:
According to the petitioners deceased was doing Labour work and he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
In this regard the petitioner has not produced any documents.
Under the circumstances, this court has to consider the notional income to assess the loss of dependency.

17. In Legal Manager IFFCO Tokio GIC Ltd., V/s Srinivasa and Others, 2018 SCC online Kar 2862 Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "the court cannot ignore the notional income chart of the Lokadalath when there is no material evidence to prove the actual income.

sentences.text:
Hence, in the absence of material on record to prove the actual income of the deceased as on the date of occurrence of accident, the charge formulated by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru is to be followed to asses the notional income of deceased as on the date of accident".
18.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru while holding Lokadalath, has determined the notional income at Rs.16,000/- if the accident had occurred in the year-2023 and thus income of the deceased is to be considered at Rs.16,000/- per month.
19. Loss of dependency:
The following issues are to be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at loss of dependency, they are (i) addition/deduction to be made for arriving at the income.
(ii) Deductions to be made towards the personal living expenses of the deceased.

20. As per the decision reported in National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Other reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "if the deceased is below 40 years 40% of the established income of deceased towards future prospectus; an addition of 25%
where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years; an addition 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as necessary method of computation."

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Other reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applying the same formula to the case on hand it is clear that, the deceased is entitled for future prospects.
In the present case the deceased is aged about 51 years and therefore 10% of the established income of the deceased is assessed towards future prospects.
Hence, the future prospects is determined as Rs.1,600/- (16,000 X 10/100 = Rs.1,600/-).

Therefore the total income of the deceased is determined as Rs.17,600/- per month (16,000 +1,600 = Rs.17,600/-).
21.
Admittedly, petitioners are the dependents of deceased person.

As per the the Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others reported in 2009 ACJ SC 1298 case, when there are 2 to 3 Dependants 1/3rd of the income is to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased.

entities.text: Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others reported in 2009 ACJ SC 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such 1/3rd amount is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses i.e., Rs.5,866/-.
When the said 1/3rd amount is deducted from monthly income of the deceased, then the balance amount shall be Rs.11,734/- (Rs.17,600 - Rs.5,866 = Rs.11,734/-).

As per the ratio laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation Ltd., and another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, the multiplier to the age of the deceased is 11.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation Ltd., and another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, total loss of income from the deceased comes to (Rs.11,734/- X 12 X 11 =Rs.15,48,888/-).
Hence, Loss of dependency is determined as Rs.15,48,888/-.
22. Transportation, Funeral expenses, Loss of Estate, Loss of love and affection and Loss of Consortium:-
In so far as the funeral and other expenses are concerned, as per the version of the petitioner he have spent Rs.80,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.
But he has not produced any documents to substantiate the said version.

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranaya Sheti and other the Compensation under the heads of transportation, funeral expenses, loss of estate, loss of love and affection and loss of consortium has to be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since, it is settled law in National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, that the dependents would be entitled for the transportation of dead body to an extent of Rs.15,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% in every three years.

Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.27,500/- i.e., (25,000 X 10/100 =Rs.2,500/- + Rs.25,000/-).
Loss of consortium:
it is pertinent to note that, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi case has directed to award an amount of Rs.40,000/- towards consortium.

Subsequently, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and others reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 has held that, the term "consortium" is compendious of spousal, parental and filial consortium and directed to award amount in all three categories.

sentences.text:
Hence,
in view of the said decisions this tribunal awards under the head of consortium as follows;
(I) Towards parental consortium: Petitioner No.1 and 2 are the son and daughter of deceased and have lost love and affection of father and hence, they are entitled for Rs.44,000/- each under this head (40,000 X 10/100 =Rs.4,000/- + Rs.40000/-).
(I) Towards filial consortium: Petitioner No.3 is the mother of deceased and have lost love and affection of son and hence, she entitled for Rs.44,000/- under this head (40,000 X 10/100 =Rs.4,000/- + Rs.40000/-).
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads.

Hence, the respondents No.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

ISSUE NO.4:-
24.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.17,57,888/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 30:40:30.
The respondent No.3 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner No.1 to 3, it is ordered to release entire amount in their favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
